pool_config.pool_brief: Build a function-based processing system for a Nigerian business context. Your solution must use: at least 3 named functions with parameters and return values, at least 1 default parameter, at least 1 arrow function, and the functions must compose (the output of one feeds as input to another). All variables must use const or let (no var).

projects.title: Konga Order Processing System
projects.scenario: Build a function-based order processing pipeline for a Konga seller. Process the provided order dataset using separate, composable functions.
requirements: Write `calculateSubtotal(orders)` — takes array of orders, returns sum of prices for non-cancelled orders
Write `applyVAT(amount, rate = 0.075)` — takes a subtotal and optional rate, returns the total with tax
Write `printOrderLine(order)` — takes a single order object, prints: `ORD-001 | Amara Obi | ₦4500 | delivered`
Write an arrow function `getStatusBadge` — takes a status string, returns 'Active', 'Pending', or 'Cancelled'
Chain the functions: loop orders with printOrderLine, then calculate subtotal and pass it to applyVAT, then print the final total

projects.title: Publica Academy Student Results Processor
projects.scenario: Build a function-based results processing system for a Publica Academy cohort. Process the provided student dataset using separate, composable functions.
requirements: Write `getGrade(score)` — returns 'Distinction' (>=80), 'Pass' (>=50), or 'Fail' using early returns
Write `calculateAverage(scores)` — takes an array of numbers, returns the average (sum / count)
Write `printStudentResult(student)` — takes a student object, prints: `Amara Obi: 88 — Pass`
Write an arrow function `isPassing` — takes a student object, returns true if score >= 50
Chain: loop students with printStudentResult, use calculateAverage to get cohort average, print how many students pass using isPassing

projects.title: PiggyVest Savings Account Manager
projects.scenario: Build a function-based savings account manager for PiggyVest. Process the provided transaction dataset using separate, composable functions.
requirements: Write `getBalance(transactions)` — sums deposits, subtracts withdrawals, returns final balance
Write `applyInterest(balance, rate = 0.08)` — returns balance plus 8% annual interest by default
Write `printTransaction(txn)` — prints: `TXN-001 | deposit | ₦5000 | savings`
Write an arrow function `isDeposit` — takes a transaction object, returns true if type is 'deposit'
Chain: loop transactions with printTransaction, calculate balance, pass to applyInterest, print final balance with interest

projects.title: Paystack Payment Analytics
projects.scenario: Build a function-based payment analytics dashboard for a Paystack merchant. Process the provided payment dataset using separate, composable functions.
requirements: Write `getTotalRevenue(payments)` — returns sum of amounts for successful payments only
Write `applyProcessingFee(amount, feeRate = 0.015)` — returns amount minus 1.5% processing fee by default
Write `printPaymentLine(payment)` — prints: `PAY-001 | Shoprite | ₦15000 | success`
Write an arrow function `isSuccessful` — takes a payment object, returns true if status is 'success'
Chain: loop payments with printPaymentLine, calculate total revenue, pass to applyProcessingFee, print net revenue

projects.title: Bolt Driver Earnings Calculator
projects.scenario: Build a function-based earnings calculator for a Bolt driver. Process the provided trips dataset using separate, composable functions.
requirements: Write `calculateGrossEarnings(trips)` — returns total fare from all trips
Write `applyCommission(amount, rate = 0.2)` — returns amount minus 20% Bolt commission by default
Write `printTripLine(trip)` — prints: `TRIP-001 | Gbenga Musa | ₦1800 | 4.8★`
Write an arrow function `isHighRated` — takes a trip object, returns true if rating >= 4.5
Chain: loop trips with printTripLine, calculate gross earnings, pass to applyCommission, print net earnings; also count and print high-rated trips using isHighRated

criteria.label: Named Functions with Parameters and Return Values

descriptors.full: All three required named functions defined correctly, each takes the right parameters, each returns the correct value (not just console.logs it)
descriptors.partial: One or two functions work correctly, remaining have errors or return undefined instead of a value
descriptors.none: Functions missing, not using parameters, or not returning values

descriptors.full: Default parameter used correctly in one function (fallback works when argument omitted), arrow function correctly defined and called
descriptors.partial: One of the two implemented correctly, the other missing or broken
descriptors.none: No default parameter used, or arrow function missing

descriptors.full: Functions chain correctly: output of one function passed as argument to another, final result computed and printed
descriptors.partial: Functions defined but not composed — results computed independently rather than chained
descriptors.none: Functions not composed; all logic written inline without using the defined functions

descriptors.full: Function names use verbs in camelCase, const/let used correctly, output format matches requirements
descriptors.partial: Minor naming issues or small formatting discrepancies
descriptors.none: var used, poor naming, or output significantly malformed
